data.gender_notes: Martina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin Martina, meaning 'Mary of martyrs'. In Christianity, Martina is the name of several saints, including Saint Martina of Rome who was martyred in the 2nd century. The name Martina carries the meaning “Mary of martyrs” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Martina usually hope their child will grow to embody mary of martyrs and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: מרטינה
in_hebrew.meaning: מרטינה היא שמה של אישה המסמלת את האלהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מרטינה נגזרת מהשם הרומי מרטינוס שפירושו המלח של אלוהים או המרטין הקדוש, שם שמקורו במילה اللاتינית 'מרס' שפירושו מלח. השם מרטינה משמש כנקבה של מרטינוס ומשדר אלוהות וקדושה.

in_greek.name: Μαρτίνα
in_greek.meaning: Μαρτίνα σημαίνει αφίσα του Άρη ή του Πολεμίου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μαρτίνα προέρχεται από το ρωμαϊκό όνομα Martinus, που σημαίνει αφίσα του Άρη ή του Πολεμίου. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο Άρης αντιπροσωπεύει τον πολεμίου πνεύμα, επομένως το όνομα Μαρτίνα φέρει πνευματική σημασία ως προς την πνευματική μάχη.

in_latin.name: Martina
in_latin.meaning: Martina means warlike or dedicated to Mars
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Martina is derived from the Roman name Martinus, which means warlike or dedicated to Mars. In early Christian tradition, the name Martina was associated with Saint Martin, a 4th-century bishop known for his piety and generosity. The name Martina conveys a sense of strength and devotion.

in_english.name: Martina
in_english.meaning: Martina means warlike or lady of war
in_english.long_meaning: The name Martina originates from the Hebrew and Greek roots, associated with the god of war, Mars. In Christian tradition, Martina is linked to Saint Martin, a 4th-century bishop. The name Martina signifies strength, courage, and devotion. It is popular across Christian cultures, symbolizing a strong and pious woman.

data.cultural_impact: The name Martina holds deep cultural significance in the Christian tradition as it is the name of several revered saints. Saint Martina of Rome is one of the most notable, whose feast day on October 12th continues to be celebrated in various parts of the world. The name Martina is also popular in countries with significant Christian populations such as Spain, Italy, and Portugal, where it is among the top 50 given names.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Martina lies in its derivation from the Latin Martina, meaning 'Mary of martyrs'. As such, the name carries the memory and legacy of Mary, the mother of Jesus, and the countless Christian martyrs who gave their lives for their faith. The name serves as a reminder of the strength and courage of these individuals in the face of adversity, inspiring those who bear the name to live boldly in their faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Martina is derived from the Latin martus, meaning "witness." A Martina, therefore, is called to bear witness to the love and truth of God in her daily life. She is a beacon of faith, shining light into the world with her courage and commitment.
